idiom_name: class with # private fields and copy-on-read views
implementation_notes: JavaScript has runtime-hard privacy: private class elements declared with `#` 'cannot be legally referenced outside of the class', so a `#lines` array and `#totalCents` counter are unreachable and the boundary is enforced by the language rather than by an underscore convention. The root mutates state only through methods and returns copies (`[...this.#lines]`, optionally `Object.freeze`d - though freezing is shallow and does not touch private elements). No standard library provides cascade or a unit of work, so the repository and the transaction stay application code (one SQL transaction or one event-store append); the classic structure is written in class syntax rather than replaced.
pitfalls: The underscore convention is not privacy: `_lines` remains a public property that serializers, decorators and any caller can read and write - use `#` for everything the root owns.
Subclasses cannot see a parent's `#` name (it is an early SyntaxError) and must not redeclare it, so extension points belong in methods rather than in protected fields.
`Object.freeze` is shallow: a frozen array of mutable line objects still lets the receiver mutate the lines, so copy the elements or freeze them at construction.
Private state is not persisted by `JSON.stringify` or structured clone defaults: mapping the aggregate to a wire format needs explicit serializers, or the parts silently disappear.
